title: Smooth purity for all admissible coefficients
statement:
Work in the standing separated finite-type $k$-scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], with the global purity datum of [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, and finite coefficient extensions inside the fixed $\Qlb$. Here admissible finite $A$ means any finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$. The categories $\Dctf$ are the pro-etale condensed-module categories of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; the twists are [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], with the finite-$A$ twist specified in [det-sp-finite-general-ring]. Integral categories are compared with completed, derived-complete categories by [sk-lem-integral-models], rational categories with scalar localizations by [det-sp-rational-localized-hom], and the $\Qlb$ category with finite condensed coefficient stages by [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]. These comparisons are equivalences, not identifications with discrete non-torsion constant-coefficient categories. Smoothness and relative dimension mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\Zl,\mathcal O_E,\Ql,E,\Qlb\}$ be any admissible coefficient
ring and let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d$. There is an
isomorphism of functors $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, given at
$K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ by a canonical isomorphism in $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$

$$
\gamma_{f,\Lambda}(K):\ f_\Lambda^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }f_\Lambda^!K.
$$

Here $f^!_\Lambda$ is the restriction of the right adjoint from
[sk-prop-sf-existence]. The isomorphism is compatible with change of
coefficients, base change and composition, with the normalization given by
integration on the affine line.

Moreover, $K\mapsto f_\Lambda^*K(d)[2d]$ is a right adjoint of
$Rf_{!,\Lambda}:\Dctf(X,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$, with counit normalized by
integration on the affine line, and $\gamma_{f,\Lambda}$ is the *unique*
isomorphism of functors $f_\Lambda^*(-)(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}f_\Lambda^!$ on
$\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ compatible with the counits of the two adjunctions.

An étale $f$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and the theorem
with $d=0$ says $f_\Lambda^!\simeq f_\Lambda^*$ for every admissible $\Lambda$. For a smooth curve $C$ with structure map
$a:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ it gives
$a_{\Zl}^!\mathbf Z_{\ell,\operatorname{Spec}k}\simeq\mathbf Z_{\ell,C}(1)[2]$, a
single sheaf in degree $-2$.

proof.text: Put $F=Rf_!$, $J=f^*(-)(d)[2d]$, and let $G=f^!$ have counit $\varepsilon$. [sk-thm-existence](2)--(4) restricts $F\dashv G$ to the categories in the statement. For finite $A$, [lem-pur-transport-finite-counit-system] supplies $F\dashv J$ with $t^A=\varepsilon^A\circ F(\gamma^A)$, the coefficient/reduction equations and geometric compatibilities, and the integration normalization; its section-action comparison makes this the same $F$, also for nonregular $A$.

Its simultaneous geometric equations and transitive coefficient comparisons supply the required integral compatibilities and integration normalization. The case $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ includes $\mathbf Z_\ell$.

It gives the representative-independent Hom bijection for rational objects and fractional arrows, the localized counit, and agreement with the specified rational purity family, including geometric equations and transitive coefficient comparisons. Thus $F\dashv J$ with its prescribed $t$ also for $E$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$.

proof.text: The rational bijections satisfy the transition hypotheses of [lem-pur-transport-qbar-common-stage-counit]. Its common-stage Hom bijection gives $F_{\Qlb}\dashv J_{\Qlb}$ with the finite-stage integration counit; its descent and conjugation assertions give geometric equations and coefficient equations for the specified exceptional adjoints.

proof.text: For every coefficient we now have the fixed adjunctions $F\dashv J$ with $t$ and $F\dashv G$ with $\varepsilon$. [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint], with its letters exchanged, yields the unique natural isomorphism $\gamma:J\to G$ satisfying $\varepsilon_K\circ F(\gamma_K)=t_K$. The comparisons in Steps 1--4 satisfy exactly this equation, so they are this same $\gamma$; their coherence and normalization therefore apply to it. For each transition among $A_{E,n}$, $\mathcal O_E$, $E$ and $\Qlb$, [det-sp-unique-adjoint-coefficients] makes the coefficient mate of the fixed $f^!$ the conjugate by these $\gamma$ of the $J$-mate, which Steps 2--4 identify with the source comparison; so the coefficient equations hold for $f^!$. Arbitrary finite $A$ is Step 1. For etale $f$, $d=0$ removes the twist and shift. For a smooth curve evaluate $\gamma^{-1}$ on $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and use [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients](1): $a^!\mathbf Z_\ell\simeq\mathbf Z_{\ell,C}(1)[2]$, a sheaf in degree $-2$. The identical substitution for a smooth $d$-fold gives the source's dualizing-complex specialization.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\Zl,\mathcal O_E,\Ql,E,\Qlb\}$ be any admissible coefficient
ring and let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d$. There is an
isomorphism of functors $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, given at
$K\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ by a canonical isomorphism in $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$

$$
\gamma_{f,\Lambda}(K):\ f_\Lambda^*K(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }f_\Lambda^!K.
$$

Here $f^!_\Lambda$ is the restriction of the right adjoint from
[sk-prop-sf-existence]. The isomorphism is compatible with change of
coefficients, base change and composition, with the normalization given by
integration on the affine line.

Moreover, $K\mapsto f_\Lambda^*K(d)[2d]$ is a right adjoint of
$Rf_{!,\Lambda}:\Dctf(X,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$, with counit normalized by
integration on the affine line, and $\gamma_{f,\Lambda}$ is the *unique*
isomorphism of functors $f_\Lambda^*(-)(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}f_\Lambda^!$ on
$\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ compatible with the counits of the two adjunctions.

For étale $f$ we have $d=0$, and the theorem says $f_\Lambda^!\simeq f_\Lambda^*$
for every admissible $\Lambda$. For a smooth curve $C$ with structure map
$a:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ it gives
$a_{\Zl}^!\mathbf Z_{\ell,\operatorname{Spec}k}\simeq\mathbf Z_{\ell,C}(1)[2]$, a
single sheaf in degree $-2$.

proof.text:
*Step 1 (compatibility with the finite reductions).* For $m\le n$
write $\mathrm{red}_{n,m}=(-)\otimes^{L}_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$. By
[sk-thm-smooth-purity] the map $\gamma_{f,K}$ is the composite of three
constituents: the canonical twist reassociation, the inverse of the
diagonal identification $\omega_f\cong\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ of
[sk-thm-smooth-purity], and the tensor formula (G11) of [sk-prop-cohsm]. Each
is compatible with $\mathrm{red}_{n,m}$: the finite-level twist
$A(1)=\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\Z/\ell^N}A$ of [sk-def-purity-conv] and the
Kummer boundary $\partial\kappa(t)$ that orients it ([sk-prop-a1]) reduce to
their counterparts over $A_{E,m}$, and the exceptional adjunction
$Rf_!\dashv Rf^{!}$ is compatible with reduction of the coefficient ring.
Hence $\mathrm{red}_{n,m}(\gamma_{f,K})=\gamma_{f,\mathrm{red}_{n,m}K}$,
and likewise for the orientations, the smooth traces and the composition
and base-change squares of [sk-prop-cohsm] (G12).

*Step 2 (the coefficients $\mathcal O_E$, $E$ and $\Qlb$).* These are the
condensed coefficient rings of [def-sf-setting], and no stage is built from
another. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, [sk-prop-sp-integral-adjunction] shows that
$K\mapsto f^*_{\mathcal O_E}K(d)[2d]$ is right adjoint to $Rf_{!,\mathcal O_E}$ on
$\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$. Its proof passes through the tower model of
[sk-prop-sp-tower-geometric] and uses the equivalence of $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$ with
normalized towers ([sk-lem-sp-tower]), a consequence of the integral criterion
[sk-prop-integral-criterion]. For $\Lambda=E$ the same holds by
[sk-prop-sp-rational], where integral models and Hom groups tensored with $E$
enter only as consequences of [sk-lem-integral-models] and
[sk-thm-sfb-rationalization-comparison]. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$ it holds by
[sk-thm-sp-qbar], where descent to a finite $E$ is
[sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit].

*Step 3 (identification with $f^!$ and uniqueness).* Both adjunctions live on
$\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$, and in both $Rf_!$ is the composite
$R\bar f_*\circ j_!$ of ordinary derived functors on module sheaves for a
compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$, independent of the compactification. Finite
purity ([sk-thm-smooth-purity]), the integral adjunction
([sk-prop-sp-integral-adjunction]) and its rational extensions
([sk-prop-sp-rational] and [sk-thm-sp-qbar]) show, in the respective
coefficient cases, that $K\mapsto f_\Lambda^*K(d)[2d]$ is right adjoint to
$Rf_{!,\Lambda}$. By [sk-prop-sf-existence] and [sk-thm-existence], the
restriction of $f^!$ is also right adjoint to $Rf_{!,\Lambda}$ on $\Dctf$.
[sk-prop-sp-unique-adjoint] gives the unique counit-preserving isomorphism from
the explicit adjoint $K\mapsto f_\Lambda^*K(d)[2d]$ to $f_\Lambda^!$.

*Step 4 (compatibility with change of coefficients).* By Step 1 and
[det-sp-purity-coefficient-change], the purity maps and smooth traces with
coefficients $\mathcal O_E$ reduce modulo $\ell^n$ (and modulo $\pi_E^n$) to
the finite ones, those with coefficients $E$ are obtained from integral models
by inverting $\ell$, and those with coefficients $\Qlb$ by extension of scalars
from a finite $E$. Applied to $f=a_X$ and $K=\Lambda_{\Spec k}$ this gives
$\omega_{X,\Lambda}\simeq\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$, with the counit normalized by
finite-level integration ([sk-cor-sp-all-coefficients]).

For every admissible $\Lambda$ the exceptional inverse image of a smooth
morphism is therefore the twisted and shifted inverse image, normalized by
integration on the affine line, and the smooth trace is the counit of
$Rf_!\dashv f^!$ in this form. It is compatible with change of coefficients
(Step 4), base change ([sk-prop-sp-purity-bc]) and composition
([sk-prop-sp-composition], [sk-prop-sp-trace-composition]).

statement_change.what: The clause 'For étale $f$ we have $d=0$' is false when $X$ is empty. By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] 'smooth of relative dimension $n$' is a condition at every point of $X$, so the empty morphism $\emptyset\to Y$ (e.g. $\emptyset\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, or the identity of the empty $k$-scheme) is étale and smooth of pure relative dimension $d$ for every $d\ge0$; with $d=1$ all hypotheses hold and $d\ne0$ (Lean: SmoothOfRelativeDimension is a universally quantified field over points of the source; checked by the stage-2 workers NY, Q03, ND, Q44, NA, N0, NK, NB on 2026-10-25, each abandoning with 'unit statement'). The functor isomorphism itself is not affected: on the empty scheme both sides lie in the zero category, so it holds for every $d$, and the uniqueness clause holds trivially. Minimal correction: the clause now says that an étale $f$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $0$ and that the theorem applied with $d=0$ gives $f^!\simeq f^*$; it no longer asserts that the given $d$ equals $0$. Nothing else changed. The current blueprint (main-20261025, blueprint_update.statement) still has the false clause; do not restore it (coord/HUMAN.md, 'Blueprint statement error: sk-thm-purity-transport').
